item.title: Activist Anson Funds Pushes Lionsgate for Sale, Semafor Says
item.description: Activist investor Anson Funds Management is urging Lionsgate Studio Corp. to put itself up for sale, Semafor reported, adding to pressure on the independent film and TV production company to do a deal.

item.title: Kenya Joins Peers in Leaving Interest Rates on Hold on Iran War
item.description: Kenya’s central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged for third time in a row as it monitors the impact of the ongoing Iran war on the economy.

item.title: Atlanta Airport Taps Munis for $1.1 Billion as Sector Sales Lag
item.description: The world’s busiest airport is coming to market with a more than $1 billion municipal bond sale, boosting issuance in the lagging airport sector.

item.title: MTN Sees First-Half Profit Jump on Nigeria, Ghana Mobile Gains
item.description: MTN Group Ltd. said adjusted first-half earnings climbed as much as 23% after improved results from the Nigerian, Ghanaian and Ugandan operations of Africa’s biggest mobile-network operator.

item.title: Chobani Cuts Annual Earnings Forecast on Rising Material Costs
item.description: Chobani has lowered its annual earnings forecast as the Greek yogurt maker contends with rising material costs, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: CSN Gets Financial Relief as $1 Billion Debt Exchange Approved
item.description: Brazil’s Cia. Siderurgica Nacional SA got enough support from holders to push through a debt exchange, getting it fresh financial relief as it struggles to cope with high financing costs.

item.title: US Previously Owned Home Sales Decline to Three-Month Low
item.description: US sales of existing homes fell to a three-month low in July as elevated prices and mortgage rates continued to weigh on the housing market.

item.title: Russia’s Crude Oil Exports Tumble to Their Lowest Since May
item.description: A brief lull in drone strikes allowed refiners to boost runs, likely diverting crude from exports

item.title: NYSE Parent ICE Looks to Raise About $3.5 Billion From Bond Sale
item.description: Intercontinental Exchange Inc. has begun the sale of US investment-grade bonds two weeks after announcing a $6 billion deal to acquire MarketAxess Holdings Inc.

item.title: Severe Thunderstorms Across US Midwest Trigger Flood Warnings
item.description: The US Midwest and Ohio Valley, including Chicago and Cincinnati, face an enhanced, or level 3, risk of severe thunderstorms.

item.title: Defense Startup Neros Triples Valuation to $2.5 Billion
item.description: Neros Inc. raised $250 million in a funding round that tripled its valuation to $2.5 billion, money that will boost the defense startup’s drone development and production to meet rising US government demand.

item.title: South Africa Vows Eskom Won’t Weaken After Transmission Restructuring
item.description: South Africa’s presidency rebuked the chairman of Eskom Holdings SOC Ltd. for publicly questioning the plan to restructure the state power utility.

item.title: Spotify Asks Creators to Label Songs When They’re AI-Generated
item.description: Spotify Technologies SA will begin identifying songs created by artificial intelligence with a new “AI Personas” label.

item.title: Buying Opportunity Forms Around S&P Skeptics’ Refusal to Give Up
item.description: US stocks may be sitting at a record, but anxiety about everything from geopolitics to inflation and a divided Federal Reserve is keeping animal spirits at bay. And that may be just what the rally needs to continue.

item.title: SNB’s US Stock Portfolio Hit New Record in Second Quarter
item.description: The value of the Swiss National Bank’s foreign-exchange reserves held in US stocks grew more than 10% in the second quarter, reaching its highest level on record.

item.title: Veritas-Backed Gainwell Kicks Off Bond Part of $5.8 Billion Deal
item.description: Gainwell Technologies has started the next leg of a broader $5.8 billion debt overhaul that marks the US software sector’s biggest financing of 2026 in the junk-debt market.

item.title: Dating App Bumble to Let Men Make the First Move With Messaging Change
item.description: Bumble Inc. will allow men to make the first move in messaging on its dating app, marking a major reversal from the company’s signature women-go-first model as it seeks to court younger users and deliver on a long-promised turnaround.

item.title: A Dozen Ships Switch Oil Outside Hormuz as Barrels Keep Flowing
item.description: A key oil supply valve from the Middle East that involves shuttle transits through the Strait of Hormuz is continuing to function in the face of a recent spate of attacks.

item.title: US Stock Futures Rise as Oil Erases Gains on Iran Optimism
item.description: US stock futures are slightly up before the bell on Tuesday as oil erased an earlier advance while traders await key inflation data for guidance on Federal Reserve interest-rate policy.

item.title: Brazil Central Bank Sees Evidence Tight Policy Is Working
item.description: Brazil’s central bank sees more evidence its tight monetary policy is working, while stressing its interest rate needs to stay restrictive as domestic demand and supply shocks continue to pressure inflation.

item.title: Trump’s Anti-Wind Crusade Is Boosting US Gas
item.description: The government has reached agreements with a string of wind developers to redirect funds toward fossil fuels.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz: What Have Iran, US Said as Efforts to Restore Traffic Stall
item.description: The future of the Strait of Hormuz, the world’s most important artery for shipping oil and natural gas, is the main sticking point in diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. Since the breakdown of a mid-June interim truce, Iranian forces have resumed attacks on vessels in the waterway, and the US has reinstated a blockade of Iranian ports.

item.title: RBI Chief Says Inflation in Check, Bolstering Rate Hold Bets
item.description: India’s inflation remains manageable, the country’s central bank chief said, reinforcing expectations that interest rates will stay on hold.

item.title: Turkish Funds Urge Action as Stock Swings Threaten MSCI Status
item.description: Turkish investment funds are urging authorities to crack down on unusual trading activity that’s sent some stock prices soaring and has put the nation at risk of exclusion from major equity benchmarks.

item.title: Sequoia Raises Its Bets on AI Startups
item.description: The venture firm tosses aside its earlier caution to boost investments in the AI race

item.title: Amazon Is in the Crosshairs of Mamdani’s NYC Worker Agenda
item.description: A New York City bill calls for the company to hire thousands of contract couriers. Amazon says the proposal will make delivery pricier and slower.

item.title: Arctic shipping routes and container carriers
item.description: Arctic route remains small and seasonal, but shows how wars and tariffs are rewiring global trade

item.title: US Moves Past Tariffs to Focus on Supply Chain Revamps in China Trade Policy
item.description: Washington has been steadily moving to revamp supply chains away from China.

item.title: India’s Retail Traders Lost $9.6 Billion in Equity Derivatives
item.description: Individuals in India lost 916.85 billion rupees ($9.6 billion) buying and selling equity futures and options in the year ended March, down from 1.1 trillion rupees a year earlier, the government told lawmakers on Tuesday.

item.title: India’s Malhotra Says BRICS Eyeing Faster Cross-Border Payments
item.description: India is working to make cross-border payments easier and cheaper while promoting local-currency settlement with its trading partners, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said.
